cases.prompt: pick a color palette and fonts for my landing page
my AI-generated site looks generic like every other SaaS, fix the design
how do I stop Cursor from producing the same purple-gradient look every time
set up a DESIGN.md so the agent builds on-brand
define design tokens for our brand
what typography and spacing should this landing page use
make the agent follow our design system instead of hardcoding hex colors
how do I enforce our brand colors so the AI doesn't drift off them
choose a distinctive visual style for our marketing page
set up lint rules that reject arbitrary colors in AI-written components
write the hero headline copy
what sections should the landing page have and in what order
add a fade-in animation on scroll
build the button component in React
run an accessibility audit for screen readers
A/B test two color variants of the CTA
improve the page's Core Web Vitals
write copy that isn't generic AI slop
scaffold a Next.js project with shadcn
our v0-generated landing page looks like every other SaaS, give it a distinctive look
expected_behavior: names the specific AI-slop tells to remove (default Inter/Poppins, blue-to-purple/aurora gradient, glassmorphism, three equal-weight card grid, centered eyebrow-pill hero)
proposes a constrained palette budget (<=4 roles, warm neutrals over pure #fff/#000, accent reserved for the CTA) and 1-2 typefaces with a >=16px body floor
warns that telling the model 'make it premium/distinctive' ratchets toward the average, and to specify concrete budgets instead

cases.prompt: set up a DESIGN.md so our coding agent stays on brand
expected_behavior: describes DESIGN.md as YAML tokens plus prose rationale, with tokens defined as roles (primary = 'main ink color') not raw hex
includes a Do's-and-Don'ts section built from real bad outputs actually seen
notes DESIGN.md is an early/alpha convention (Google Labs, 2026) to verify against the current spec, not a ratified cross-tool standard
recommends keeping visual spec in DESIGN.md, separate from behavioral rules in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md

cases.prompt: how do I make sure the AI actually uses our tokens and doesn't hardcode colors
expected_behavior: recommends deterministic enforcement gates over prose (ESLint no-arbitrary-colors / no-restricted-imports, Stylelint declaration-strict-value, TS discriminated unions for variants, visual-regression + axe-core in CI)
explains enforcement beats prose because written rules get dropped under deadline
caps the self-correction loop and forbids the agent editing lint config, adding eslint-disable, or minting a new token to dodge a rule

cases.prompt: just give me the brand hex codes, that's all the agent needs
expected_behavior: pushes back that raw token values without usage rules just relocate the problem
explains the agent also needs roles, prose judgment, and a Don'ts list, not only hex values
notes a pure token dump still produces technically-correct but off-brand output
